task_name: the go stops asking whether the plan is under review

rubric.result: The objective promises two things and the diff produces both. (1) «the go is admitted with no plan review consulted»: `#accept` loses the `ReviewGatePolicy` call and both refusal branches (`if (inFlight === ReviewInFlight.IN_FLIGHT)` and the UNREADABLE stderr warning), `#reviewInFlight` and `#reworking` are deleted, `handledBy` and `#accept` lose the `readPlanProgress` parameter, `api-server.ts` loses the collaborator, the field and the `PlanProgressReader` type, `ct-api.ts` stops passing it to `ApiServer` while keeping the local that feeds `#planEvents`, `ReviewWatch.refresh()` goes and `backend/src/domain/policies/review-gate-policy.ts` is deleted. Nothing left in `backend/src` names `refresh`, `ReviewInFlight` or `ReviewGatePolicy`. (2) «`plan-under-review` retires on both halves of the wire»: the backend drops `ImplementRequestOutcome.PLAN_UNDER_REVIEW` and its `ImplementRefusal` entry; the frontend drops `{ kind: 'under-review' }` from `ImplementPlanOutcome`, the `PLAN_UNDER_REVIEW` constant and the branch that mapped it in `client.ts`, `UNDER_REVIEW_TITLE`/`UNDER_REVIEW_DESCRIPTION` and the banner in `ImplementPlanAction.tsx`, and `ImplementPlanMother.planUnderReview`. Both halves travel in this one diff.

The **TDD:** line asks for `it('a_plan_whose_progress_nobody_asks_about_still_admits_the_go')` in `implement-plan-route.test.ts`, «with no progress reader wired the route answers 202 and `RunningApi.spy.asked` holds the request». The diff adds exactly that test: `RunningApi.listening()` (whose `ApiServer` literal no longer carries `readPlanProgress`), one POST of `RunningApi.ACCEPTED_BODY`, `expect(response.status).toBe(202)` and `expect(RunningApi.spy.asked).toEqual([{ agent: 'workspace:20', issue: 33, repository: 'jjponz/repo-pulse' }])`. Same input, same assertion, same expected value as the written phrase.

The `Contract (backend/src/infrastructure/implement-plan-route.ts)` block states the frozen `ImplementRequestOutcome` with eight members and `type PlanReviews = { stop(watched: WatchedIssue): void }`. The diff states both literally: the vocabulary keeps ACCEPTED, BODY_NOT_A_JSON_OBJECT, UNKNOWN_FIELD, MALFORMED_AGENT, MALFORMED_ISSUE, MALFORMED_REPO, NO_LIVE_SESSION and UNCERTAIN_PHASE with their kebab-case values unchanged and loses only PLAN_UNDER_REVIEW, and `PlanReviews` collapses to the single-method shape the block writes. The `Current state` block (lines 346-353, `#reviewInFlight`) is exactly the hunk the diff deletes. The §2 row «What `ImplementPlanRoute.handledBy` ends as» describes the end of the slice, not of this task — its own companion rows say the `reviews` argument goes in Task 4 — so keeping `reviews` in `handledBy` is the contract this task was given, and the Contract block's `PlanReviews` confirms it.

Rows the diff bears on, each implemented with the value the row states: «What goes in Task 3, file by file» — `implement-plan-route.ts` loses `#reviewInFlight`, `#reworking` and the `readPlanProgress` parameter of `handledBy`/`#accept`; `api-server.ts` loses the collaborator, the field and `PlanProgressReader`; `ct-api.ts` loses `readPlanProgress` from the `ApiServer` arguments and keeps the local feeding `#planEvents`; `review-watch.ts` loses `refresh()` and its `ReviewInFlight` import; `reviews-spy.ts` loses `inFlight`, `refresh`, `withAnUndeliveredChange` and `unreadable`; `ImplementPlan.types.ts`, `client.ts`, `ImplementPlanAction.tsx` and `ImplementPlanMother.ts` lose exactly what the row names. «What `ImplementPlanRoute` loses» — obeyed including its own clause that `reviews.stop(...)` goes with Task 4. «What `ReviewWatch` loses» — only `refresh()` and the import; `start`, `startRecovered`, `stop`, `log`, `#note` and the six named constructor arguments are untouched. «Which modules are deleted, not deprecated» — `review-gate-policy.ts` is deleted, not emptied. «Where the two halves of a contract move together» — `plan-under-review` leaves backend and frontend in this one commit. «Which suite covers the surviving watch» — `pull-request-review-loop.test.ts` is not among the touched paths, and `CtApi.#pullRequestReviews` is untouched as `### Out of scope` demands. One removal beyond the rows: `ReviewsSpy.asked`, which only the deleted `refresh` ever wrote and which the removed tests were its only readers; that follows `conventions/simplicity.md` rather than reopening a row.

Exemplars: `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/implement-history-route.test.ts` — the edited route test keeps that shape (a real `ApiServer` on port 0, a real `fetch`, the use case doubled by construction, `afterEach` stopping every server); `implement-history-route.ts`'s `Projection`-backed refusal vocabulary — `ImplementRefusal.#BY_OUTCOME` stays a `Projection` map that loses one entry with no catch-all added and `declaredOutcomes()` untouched; `ImplementProgress.tsx` — `ImplementPlanAction.tsx` now renders `implementing/refused/stale-agent/uncertain/backend-unreachable` with no retired member left. Rules: `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` — every identifier and test name added is English and the only Spanish text removed is frontend product copy (the banner's title and description), which is the one exemption; no control was routed around (all six verification commands exit 0 in the log). `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` — the `{code, detail}` doctrine is untouched (the removed refusal was one of it), the layout keeps one `<endpoint>-route.ts` per endpoint, nothing leaves TypeScript, and the new test closes its server in `afterEach` («a failing test must not leak a process»). `backend/API.md` still documents `plan-under-review`, and a later task of this plan owns that line (`test "$(grep -c plan-under-review backend/API.md)" -eq 0`), so editing it here would have been out of scope. ct's yardstick: `simplicity.md` — the diff is almost pure subtraction and leaves no symbol without a caller (`#sound` still serves `#follow`/`#baseline`, `stderr` still serves the `implementationStarts.remember` failure, `CtApi.#readPlanProgress` still feeds `#planEvents`); the `ReviewLog.lastAskedAt`/`MemoryReviewLog` burden is declared in `### Out of scope` and left to a person, which is what «Where the burden cannot be discharged, that is declared» asks. `decisions.md` — «The two halves of a contract that crosses a process boundary have to exist twice… changed on both sides at once»: the `plan-under-review` code leaves `ImplementRequestOutcome` and `client.ts` in the same diff. `architecture.md` — a domain policy is deleted, no new module or concept is born, infrastructure stops importing that policy and the layer direction is unchanged. `boundaries.md` — the outward projection stays exhaustive and raising (`ImplementCollapse.of` still throws «no refusal declared»), and the answer's `code` stays declared beside its detail. `domain.md` — no port, value object or exception is named for a tool; `PlanReviews` shrinks to what is asked of the collaborator. `style.md` — no comment or docstring added, no new module-level function (the pre-existing `const implement` in `client.ts` only loses a branch). `testing.md` — the new controller test asserts the status of a real answer and what the doubled use case received. Its one tension: «Before adding a test, check whether the behaviour is already covered» — the new test's assertions are the union of the surviving `an_accepted_order_answers_that_the_implementation_is_under_way` and `the_three_fields_reach_the_use_case_as_domain_values_and_not_as_the_raw_json`, so its distinct dimension is only its name; the plan's **TDD:** line ordered that exact test with that exact assertion, so the implementer could not both obey the control and satisfy the document. Declared here and left out of the findings. `defects.md`, rule by rule: closed vocabulary — it has a subject (`ImplementRequestOutcome` and its `Projection` dispatch) and it holds: a member leaves the frozen vocabulary, the dispatch stays exhaustive and no catch-all or loose string is introduced (the frontend's generic `refused` branch is pre-existing and only loses a case above it). Raw map as the return value of logic — no subject: nothing in the diff adds a return value, and the deleted `ReviewGatePolicy.of({watched, reworking})` took a named parameters object, not a map handed on. Two fields that have to agree — no subject added; the diff in fact removes the pair `ReviewsSpy.inFlight`/`asked` and the two signals `ReviewGatePolicy` had to reconcile, and introduces no sentinel or flag. Error named for where it happens — no subject: no error is added, and the two generic `Error`s of the deleted policy leave with it.

Every pre-existing test the diff removes traces to the task's own text. The **Tests:** line names seven by name plus «the `refresh` cases of `review-watch.test.ts`, the `under-review` cases of `client.test.ts` and `ImplementPlanAction.test.tsx`»; the rest of the removed backend cases (`a_change_the_watch_has_not_delivered_yet_refuses_the_go`, `an_undelivered_change_neither_records_the_go_nor_resumes_the_agent_nor_lifts_the_watch`, `a_plan_still_being_written_is_not_under_review_and_the_go_is_admitted`, `a_plan_already_implementing_answers_the_same_202_even_while_a_review_is_in_flight`, `a_watch_that_could_not_be_asked…`, `a_state_that_could_not_be_read…`, `a_readable_signal_that_says_nothing_is_in_flight_warns_about_nothing`, `a_bug_reading_the_state_is_not_swallowed_as_an_unreadable_signal`, `the_watch_is_lifted_only_after_the_gate_found_nothing_waiting` and the four surviving `ReviewGatePolicy` unit cases) each assert behaviour the Objective retires or a module the §2 row «Which modules are deleted, not deprecated» deletes, and the Contract block removes the `PLAN_UNDER_REVIEW` member those assertions were written against. The `WatchDouble` parking scaffolding (`parking`, `parked`, `wakeParked`, `#NEVER_WAKES`, `parkedBeforeItsFirstSweep`, `parkedAfterOneSweep`, `parkedMidSleep`) existed only for the `refresh` cases and nothing in the surviving file names it. No surviving production line lost its only assertion: `reviews.stop(...)` is still pinned by `accepting_the_implementation_stops_watching_the_plan_because_that_gate_is_closed` (implement-plan-route.test.ts:357), the `ActivePlanPhase.IMPLEMENTING` short circuit by `a_duplicate_order_returns_the_same_answer_and_executes_only_once`, and the generic `request-failed` answer by the case at line 274. No assertion was relaxed in a test that stays.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code, not by scaffolding: the go is admitted because `#accept` in `backend/src/infrastructure/implement-plan-route.ts` no longer computes `#reviewInFlight` and no longer has a `PLAN_UNDER_REVIEW` branch, and `plan-under-review` is unreachable because the member left the frozen vocabulary and `client.ts` no longer maps it. Reverting the production hunks while keeping the test file would leave `handledBy` calling `reviews.refresh(...)` on a `ReviewsSpy` that no longer has it, so the new test fails — its green comes from the production lines of this diff.

Inside the declared files the diff writes only what the task asks for: the removals enumerated in the §2 row for Task 3, plus `ReviewsSpy.asked`, the field the deleted `refresh` was the only writer of. Nothing named in `### Out of scope` is touched — `ReadFixesAsked`, `RequestFixes`, `CtApi.#pullRequestReviews`, the go protocol's own modules, `GATES.plan`, `POST /implement-plan`'s routing and `cmux-plan-agents.ts` all stand, and `ReadPlanProgress` keeps its `reviewLog`/`#underReview` for the later task that owns them. The AMENDMENT is justified: the implementer added `external-tools-route.test.ts`, `implement-history-route.test.ts` and `implement-progress-route.test.ts` to **Files:**, and each change inside them is the single line `readPlanProgress: null,` removed from an `ApiServer({…})` literal. The task's own §2 row orders `api-server.ts` to lose the `readPlanProgress` entry of `ApiCollaborators`, and the task's own **Verification:** runs `npm --prefix backend run typecheck`, which TypeScript fails on those three object literals the moment the key stops existing — so the sentence of the task forces exactly those three edits and no more. The amendment adds routes and removes none; it does not touch this task's **Tests:**, **TDD:**, block declarations or **Verification:** commands, and the plan hunk contains nothing but that one rewritten **Files:** line.

One test is added, `a_plan_whose_progress_nobody_asks_about_still_admits_the_go`, and it has the three properties. Deterministic: a real server on port 0 and a real `fetch` to 127.0.0.1, no clock, no date, no randomness, no sleep, no path outside the process. Isolated: `RunningApi.listening()` rebuilds the spy, the sessions, the active plans and the server for this test alone, the file's `afterEach` stops every server it started, and the test depends on no order (it passes whether or not the cases around it ran). Verifies real behaviour: the assertion is on the status of a real HTTP answer and on the parameters the doubled use case received, and it would fail with the production hunks of this diff reverted, because `handledBy` would then call `reviews.refresh(...)` on a spy that no longer declares it. The finer half was measured with `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development`, which loaded: its «Test passes immediately? You're testing existing behavior» is the only sentence with a subject here, and it bears on the near-duplication already declared under `patrones` — the plan's **TDD:** line ordered this test verbatim, so it is reported nowhere rather than twice.
